(d) The territorial extent of the assignment is worldwide. This is stated expressly because, under Section 19(6), an assignment that does not specify its territorial extent is presumed to extend only within India.
(e) The assignment does not lapse if the Assignee does not exercise the rights within one year of the date of this Agreement, and this clause is the express provision to the contrary that Section 19(4) contemplates.
(f) This assignment is in writing and signed by the Assignor, as Section 19(1) requires for the assignment to be valid.
authoring_note: Limbs (c), (d) and (e) exist solely to displace the statutory defaults, and each says so. This is the most frequently botched assignment in Indian practice: a clause reading 'the Assignor hereby assigns all right, title and interest' without stating duration and territory gives the assignee five years within India, which is almost never what either party intended. The Organisation has constituted an Internal Committee under Section 4 of the Act at each workplace employing ten or more employees.
(a) The Presiding Officer is {{posh_presiding_officer}}, a woman employed at a senior level at the workplace.
(b) Not fewer than two members are drawn from among the employees, preferably committed to the cause of women, or having experience in social work, or having legal knowledge.
(c) The external member is {{posh_external_member}}, drawn from a non-governmental organisation or association committed to the cause of women, or being a person familiar with issues relating to sexual harassment.
(d) Not fewer than one half of the total members of the Committee are women.

title: Making a Complaint
citations: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.9; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.10
text:
An aggrieved woman may make a complaint of sexual harassment to the Internal Committee as follows.
(a) The complaint shall be made in writing, and shall be made within three months of the date of the incident, or within three months of the date of the last incident where there is a series of incidents.
(b) The Committee may extend that period by a further period not exceeding three months, where it is satisfied that circumstances prevented the complaint being made in time, and shall record its reasons in writing for doing so.
(c) Where the aggrieved woman is unable to make a complaint in writing, the Presiding Officer or any member of the Committee shall render all reasonable assistance to enable her to do so.
(d) Where the aggrieved woman is unable to make a complaint by reason of physical or mental incapacity, or death, a complaint may be made by such person as the Act permits.
(e) Before initiating an inquiry, and at the request of the aggrieved woman, the Committee may take steps to settle the matter by conciliation. No monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation. Where a settlement is arrived at, no further inquiry shall be conducted.
(f) The Organisation shall not require the aggrieved woman to attempt conciliation, and her declining it shall not count against her in any way.
authoring_note: Limb (f) is not in the Act in those words; it is drawn from Section 10, which makes conciliation available only at the aggrieved woman's request. It is stated expressly because in practice conciliation is often presented to a complainant as the expected first step. The advocate should confirm they are content for the policy to say this plainly.

title: Action and Reporting
citations: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.13; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.14; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.19; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.21; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.22; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.26; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 s.75
text:
The Organisation shall act on the recommendations of the Internal Committee as follows.
(a) Where the allegation is proved, the Organisation shall act on the Committee's recommendation within sixty days of receiving it. Sexual harassment is misconduct under the Organisation's service rules, and action may include a written warning, withholding of a promotion or increment, suspension, or termination of service.
(b) The Committee may recommend that a sum be deducted from the respondent's salary and paid to the aggrieved woman, or to her legal heirs, as compensation determined on the basis set out in the Act.
(c) Where the Committee concludes that a complaint was malicious, or that the complainant knowingly made a false allegation or produced a forged or misleading document, it may recommend action against her. The mere inability to substantiate a complaint, or to provide adequate proof, does not attract action under this sub-clause.
(d) The Organisation shall assist the aggrieved woman, if she so wishes, in making a complaint under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Section 75 of which makes sexual harassment a criminal offence, and shall initiate action against a respondent who is not an employee.
(e) The Internal Committee shall prepare an annual report and submit it to the Organisation and to the District Officer, and the Organisation shall include in its annual report the number of cases filed and disposed of.
(f) The Organisation shall organise awareness programmes for employees and orientation programmes for members of the Internal Committee, and shall display at a conspicuous place the penal consequences of sexual harassment and the constitution of the Committee.
(g) Failure by the Organisation to comply with the Act is punishable with a fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees, and on a repetition may attract twice that punishment and cancellation of its registration or licence.
authoring_note: The second sentence of limb (c) is the important one and is taken almost verbatim from Section 14: an inability to substantiate is expressly not a false complaint. Without it, a false-complaint provision reads as a deterrent to complaining at all. Limb (d) cites the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 s.75, which replaced Section 354A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 when the Sanhita commenced on 1 July 2024; the advocate should confirm the section number against the bare text. Limb (g) states the penalty on the Organisation deliberately, so that the policy is read by those who must operate it as carrying consequences.

title: Inquiry and Interim Relief

Where the matter is not settled by conciliation, the Internal Committee shall inquire into the complaint.
(a) The inquiry shall be conducted in accordance with the principles of natural justice, and shall be completed within ninety days.
(b) During the pendency of the inquiry, the Committee may, on the written request of the aggrieved woman, recommend that she be transferred to another workplace, that the respondent be transferred, that she be granted leave of up to three months in addition to her entitled leave, or that the respondent be restrained from reporting on her work performance.
(c) Leave granted as interim relief is paid leave, and shall not be deducted from the aggrieved woman's leave entitlement.
(d) The Committee shall submit its report to the Organisation within ten days of completing the inquiry, and the report shall be made available to both parties.
(e) The identity and address of the aggrieved woman, the respondent, and the witnesses, the contents of the complaint, the inquiry proceedings, and the recommendations of the Committee shall not be published or made known to the public, the press, or the media in any manner. A person who breaches this obligation is liable to the penalty under Section 17 of the Act.
(f) The Organisation shall not victimise, and shall not permit the victimisation of, any person for making a complaint, for giving evidence, or for assisting in an inquiry.

title: Scope and Definitions
citations: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.2(f); Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.2(n); Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.2(o); Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.3
text:
This Policy is adopted by {{company_name}}, of {{company_address}}, in discharge of its obligations under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, with effect from {{effective_date}} (the "Effective Date"). It applies at every workplace of the Organisation.
(a) The Policy applies to every employee, and 'employee' is used in the sense given by Section 2(f) of the Act: it includes a person engaged on a regular, temporary, ad hoc, or daily wage basis, whether directly or through an agent, whether for remuneration or not, and includes a co-worker, a contract worker, a probationer, a trainee, an apprentice, and an intern.
(b) 'Workplace' is used in the sense given by Section 2(o) of the Act, and includes any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment, including transport provided by the Organisation for the journey.
(c) 'Sexual harassment' is used in the sense given by Section 2(n) of the Act, and includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behaviour, whether directly or by implication: physical contact and advances; a demand or request for sexual favours; sexually coloured remarks; showing pornography; and any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
(d) The circumstances set out in Section 3(2) of the Act, if they occur in relation to any act of sexual harassment, may amount to sexual harassment: an implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment; an implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment; an implied or explicit threat about present or future employment status; interference with work, or the creation of an intimidating, offensive, or hostile working environment; and humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety.
(e) No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace of the Organisation.

Date: {{effective_date}} (the "Effective Date")
KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS that I/We, {{party_1_descriptor}} (the "Principal"), do hereby nominate, constitute, and appoint {{party_2_descriptor}} (the "Attorney"), to be my/our true and lawful attorney, to do and execute the acts set out in this deed in my/our name and on my/our behalf.

title: Execution and Formalities
citations: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.17; Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.18; Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.Schedule I, Article 48; Registration Act, 1908 s.17; Registration Act, 1908 s.33; Notaries Act, 1952 s.8
text:
This deed is executed subject to the following formalities.
(a) This deed is chargeable with stamp duty under Article 48 of Schedule I to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, read with the stamp law of the State in which it is executed, and must be stamped before or at the time of execution.
(b) This deed shall be signed by the Principal in the presence of two witnesses, who shall attest it.
(c) This deed shall be notarised by a Notary appointed under the Notaries Act, 1952. A notarised power of attorney carries a presumption under Section 85 of the Indian Evidence Act as to its due execution and authentication.
(d) Where this deed empowers the Attorney to present a document for registration, it must be executed and authenticated in the manner Section 33 of the Registration Act, 1908 requires, failing which the Sub-Registrar will not recognise the Attorney.
(e) Where this deed relates to immovable property and creates or transfers an interest in it, registration is compulsory under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908.
(f) Where the Principal is outside India, this deed shall be executed before, and authenticated by, a Notary Public, an Indian Consular Officer, or such other authority as Section 33 of the Registration Act, 1908 recognises, and shall be adjudicated and stamped in India within three months of being received in India, as Section 18 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 requires.
authoring_note: Limb (f) covers the non-resident case, which is the commonest use of this instrument in Indian practice and the one most often executed defectively. Section 18 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 gives three months from receipt in India, and a deed that misses it is not duly stamped. The Section 85 presumption in limb (c) should be confirmed by the advocate against the current evidence statute, since the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 has been replaced by the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and the corresponding section number may differ.

title: Limitations
citations: Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.211; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.213; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.215; Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s.54; Registration Act, 1908 s.17
text:
The Attorney's authority is subject to the following limitations.
(a) The Attorney shall act in good faith, in the interests of the Principal, and within the authority expressly conferred by this deed.
(b) The Attorney shall not delegate this authority to any other person, and shall not appoint a substitute attorney.
(c) The Attorney shall not make any gift of the Principal's property, and shall not deal with the Principal's property for the Attorney's own benefit or the benefit of a person connected with the Attorney, unless this deed expressly says so.
(d) This deed does not transfer, and shall not be construed as transferring, any right, title, or interest in immovable property to the Attorney. A transfer of immovable property is effected only by a registered instrument of conveyance, and a power of attorney is not such an instrument.
(e) The Attorney shall keep proper accounts of everything done under this deed and of all money received and paid, and shall render them to the Principal on demand.
(f) The Attorney shall keep the Principal's money separate from the Attorney's own.
authoring_note: Limb (d) states the rule in Suraj Lamp and Industries Private Limited v State of Haryana, in which the Supreme Court held that a transfer by way of sale agreement, general power of attorney and will does not convey title, and that immovable property can be transferred only by a registered deed of conveyance. The practice of using a general power of attorney as a substitute for a sale deed remains widespread notwithstanding that decision, and stating the position in the instrument itself is the clearest protection available to a principal who does not intend a transfer. The advocate should confirm the citation and consider whether a stronger recital is warranted where the powers granted relate to immovable property.

title: Intellectual Property

Each Founder assigns to the Company every right in the intellectual property described below, and shall do whatever is necessary to give effect to the assignment.
(a) Every invention, work, design, mark, database, and item of source code made by a Founder in connection with the business of the Company, whether before or after the date of this Agreement, vests in the Company.
(b) Where any such intellectual property was created before the Company was incorporated, each Founder assigns it to the Company with effect from incorporation, and this Agreement is the writing signed by the assignor that Section 19(1) of the Copyright Act, 1957 requires.

The Founders hold equity in the Company in the proportions stated in this Agreement, subject to vesting as follows.
(a) The shareholding of each Founder is: {{founder_equity_split}}.
(b) The shares held by each Founder vest over {{vesting_period}} from the Vesting Commencement Date, subject to a cliff of {{vesting_cliff}}. title: Personal Data Breach
citations: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 s.8(6); Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 s.7

(a) The Processor shall notify the Fiduciary without undue delay, and in any event within twenty-four hours of becoming aware of the breach.
(b) The notification shall describe the nature and extent of the breach, the personal data and the Data Principals affected so far as known, the likely consequences, the measures taken or proposed to mitigate it, and the person from whom further information may be obtained.

(e) The Processor shall preserve all evidence relating to the breach and shall bear its own costs of investigation and remediation.

title: Stamping and Execution
citations: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.17; Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.35; Indian Stamp Act, 1899 s.Schedule I, Article 49
text:
This Note is chargeable with stamp duty under Article 49 of Schedule I to the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, and the following applies to it.
(a) This Note must be stamped before or at the time of execution, as Section 17 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 requires. Stamp duty on a promissory note is levied under the Indian Stamp Act as a Union subject, and not under a State stamp enactment.
(b) An unstamped or insufficiently stamped promissory note CANNOT be admitted in evidence, and the defect cannot be cured afterwards by paying the duty and a penalty. Proviso (a) to Section 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 permits that cure for instruments generally, but expressly excludes a bill of exchange and a promissory note from it.
(c) The Maker is responsible for ensuring this Note is duly stamped before signing it.
(d) This Note is signed by the Maker in the presence of the witnesses whose signatures appear below.
authoring_note: This clause carries the single most consequential rule about this instrument and is written in plain terms for that reason. For most documents an unstamped instrument is a fixable problem: pay the duty and a penalty and it becomes admissible. For a promissory note it is NOT. Proviso (a) to Section 35 opens with the words 'not being an instrument chargeable with a duty of one anna or half an anna only, or a bill of exchange or promissory note', which puts this instrument outside the cure. An unstamped note is therefore worthless as evidence of the debt, permanently. Confirmed against the Punjab and Haryana High Court Rules and Orders, Volume IV, Chapter 4, Part D. The advocate should confirm the current Article 49 rate and whether it is ad valorem or fixed for the amount in question.

title: Taxation
citations: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.17(2)(vi); Income-tax Act, 1961 s.192; Income-tax Act, 1961 s.192(1C); Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80-IAC; Income-tax Act, 1961 s.49(2AA)
text:
The Optionee is responsible for the tax consequences of the options, and the following is recorded for information and is not tax advice.
(a) On exercise, the difference between the fair market value of the shares on the date of exercise and the exercise price paid is a perquisite chargeable to tax as salary under Section 17(2)(vi) of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
(b) The Company shall deduct tax at source on that perquisite under Section 192 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the Optionee shall put the Company in funds for it if the Optionee's salary is insufficient.
(c) Where the Company is an eligible start-up referred to in Section 80-IAC of the Income-tax Act, 1961, the deduction and payment of tax on the perquisite may be deferred as Section 192(1C) of that Act permits, and the Company shall inform the Optionee whether the deferral applies to this grant.
(d) On a subsequent sale of the shares, the difference between the sale consideration and the fair market value taken into account under sub-clause (a) is chargeable as capital gains.
(e) The fair market value for the purposes of sub-clause (a) is determined in the manner prescribed under the Income-tax Rules, 1962.
(f) The Optionee should take independent tax advice before exercising.
authoring_note: Tax on exercise, not on sale, is the feature of the Indian regime that most damages employees: the charge arises when the option is exercised even though the shares cannot be sold, so an employee can owe tax on a gain they cannot realise. Sub-clause (c) records the Section 192(1C) deferral available to eligible start-ups, which is the principal relief. The advocate should confirm whether this company is an eligible start-up under Section 80-IAC before the letter is issued, and should confirm the Section 49(2AA) citation for the capital gains cost base.

title: Departing Founders
citations: Companies Act, 2013 s.247; Companies Act, 2013 s.2(68); Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.74
text:
Where a Founder ceases to be engaged in the business of the Company, the following applies.
(a) A Founder is a Good Leaver where the Founder ceases to be engaged by reason of death, permanent incapacity, or a resignation the other Founders agree in writing to treat as such, or where the Founder is removed otherwise than for cause.
(b) A Founder is a Bad Leaver in every other case, including resignation before the end of the vesting period and removal for cause. Cause means a material breach of this Agreement, a breach of the duty of good faith, fraud, or conviction of an offence involving moral turpitude.
(c) A Good Leaver retains their vested shares. Their unvested shares may be acquired at fair market value, determined by a registered valuer appointed under Section 247 of the Companies Act, 2013.
(d) A Bad Leaver retains their vested shares. Their unvested shares may be acquired at the lower of the price the Founder paid for them and their fair market value.
(e) A departing Founder shall resign from the Board and from every office held in the Company with effect from the date of cessation, and shall return all property and confidential information of the Company.
(f) The obligations of a departing Founder as to confidentiality, and as to the assignment of intellectual property, continue after cessation.
authoring_note: Limb (d) prices bad-leaver shares at the LOWER of cost and fair value, and does not forfeit them outright. Outright forfeiture, or a nominal price, is vulnerable under Section 74 of the Contract Act as a penalty. The advocate should take a view on whether the definition of cause in limb (b) is tight enough, since it is the pivot on which a founder's entire holding turns and is the most litigated term in this kind of agreement.

title: Exclusivity and Confidentiality
citations: Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.27; Specific Relief Act, 1963 s.41; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.73
text:
The following provisions are binding on the Parties.
(a) For {{exclusivity_period}} from the date of this Term Sheet, the Company and the Founders shall not solicit, entertain, or negotiate any offer of investment in, or acquisition of, the Company from any other person, and shall inform the Investor of any approach received.
(b) Each Party shall keep confidential the existence and the terms of this Term Sheet, and any information disclosed in connection with it, and shall not disclose it except to its professional advisers, or as required by law or by a regulator.
(c) The exclusivity in sub-clause (a) ends if the Investor notifies the Company that it will not proceed, or on the expiry of the period, whichever is earlier.
(d) Each Party bears its own costs of negotiating and documenting the proposed investment. Where the definitive agreements provide for the Company to bear the Investor's costs, that obligation arises only on completion and is capped at the amount the definitive agreements state.
(e) A breach of sub-clause (a) or (b) may be restrained by injunction, damages alone being an inadequate remedy.
authoring_note: Sub-clause (d) is drafted to protect the company. A term sheet that obliges the company to pay the investor's legal costs regardless of completion leaves a start-up paying for a deal that never happened, and is a term founders accept without noticing. The advocate should set the exclusivity period; thirty to sixty days is usual, and an open-ended period is both commercially unreasonable and more vulnerable under Section 27.

title: Liquidation Preference
citations: Companies Act, 2013 s.43; Companies Act, 2013 s.47; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 s.53
text:
On a Liquidity Event, the proceeds available for distribution shall be applied as follows.
(a) Liquidity Event means a winding up of the Company, a sale of all or substantially all of its assets, or a sale or transfer of shares resulting in a change of control of the Company.
(b) The Investor shall receive, in priority to the holders of equity shares, an amount equal to {{liquidation_preference_multiple}} times the amount invested, together with any declared but unpaid dividend.
(c) The preference is non-participating: after receiving the amount in sub-clause (b), the Investor does not share further in the remaining proceeds, but may instead elect to convert into equity shares and take its pro rata share of the whole, whichever produces the greater amount.
(d) The balance of the proceeds is distributed among the holders of equity shares in proportion to their shareholding.
(e) A distribution on a winding up is subject to Section 53 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 where that Code applies, and the priority in this clause operates only among shareholders and does not affect the rights of creditors.
authoring_note: Sub-clause (e) exists because a liquidation preference is often written as though it ranked ahead of everything. It does not: on a winding up Section 53 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 places equity holders last, and the preference operates only in the distribution among shareholders. The advocate should decide whether a participating preference is intended, since the difference between participating and non-participating is the single largest economic term in the document and is frequently misunderstood by founders.

(b) {{company_name}} shall give the consumer a means of tracking the shipment once it is dispatched.

A consumer may return goods as follows.

title: Release and Discharge
citations: Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.63; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.23; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.28; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 s.2(f)
text:
On receipt of the full and final settlement amount, and subject to the following, each Party releases and discharges the other from every claim arising out of the employment or its ending.
(a) The Employee confirms that the settlement amount represents everything due to the Employee in respect of salary, allowances, leave, bonus, gratuity, reimbursement, and every other head arising out of the employment.
(b) The Employer releases the Employee from every claim arising out of the employment, other than a claim founded on fraud, on wilful misconduct, or on a breach of the surviving obligations recorded in this Agreement.
(c) This release does not extend to, and nothing in this Agreement shall be read as waiving, any right or remedy that the law does not permit to be waived, including any accrued statutory entitlement and any right under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.
(d) This release does not affect the Employee's right to a provident fund or pension benefit held by a statutory authority rather than by the Employer.
(e) The release takes effect only when the settlement amount is received in cleared funds.
authoring_note: Sub-clauses (c) and (d) are carve-outs from the release and are the reason this clause is drafted at length rather than as a single sentence. A release that purports to extinguish accrued statutory dues, or to bar a POSH complaint, is not merely unenforceable as to that part: it invites a finding that the whole settlement was obtained improperly. Limb (e) makes the release conditional on actual receipt, so an employee who signs and is not paid is not left having given up their claims for nothing. The advocate should confirm the list of non-waivable rights in limb (c) is complete for the employer's sector.

(a) The Maker fails to pay any sum due under this Note on its due date, and the failure continues for {{cure_period_days}} days after the Payee gives written notice of it.
(b) The Maker becomes unable to pay its debts, or a proceeding for insolvency, bankruptcy, or winding up is commenced against the Maker and is not withdrawn or dismissed within sixty days.
(c) Any statement the Maker has made to the Payee in connection with this Note proves to have been untrue in a material respect when made.

(b) Interest shall be paid {{interest_payment_frequency}}, and any interest not paid when due shall itself carry interest at the same rate.

title: Author's Special Rights
citations: Copyright Act, 1957 s.57
text:
The Parties record the following about the author's special rights.
(a) Section 57 of the Copyright Act, 1957 confers on the author of a work the right to claim authorship of it, and the right to restrain or claim damages for a distortion, mutilation, modification, or other act in relation to the work that would be prejudicial to the author's honour or reputation.
(b) Those rights are independent of the copyright and remain with the author notwithstanding this assignment. Nothing in this Agreement assigns, waives, or purports to waive them.
(c) The Assignee shall, where it is reasonable in the medium used, identify the author as the author of the work.
(d) The Assignee may edit, adapt, translate, and format the work as the exercise of the assigned rights requires, and the Assignor confirms that ordinary editorial and technical adaptation of that kind is not of itself prejudicial to the author's honour or reputation.

This clause therefore acknowledges the rights rather than attempting to acquire them, and limb (d) achieves the commercially necessary result by narrowing what counts as prejudicial, which is the defensible route. Whether a waiver is possible at all is contested; the advocate should take a view.

text: The Borrower shall provide and keep updated all documents and information required by the Lender to discharge its obligations under the Reserve Bank of India's Know Your Customer (KYC) Directions and the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002, including proof of identity, address, beneficial ownership, and source of funds. The Lender shall process such information in accordance with applicable RBI directions and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and shall maintain records for the period required by law. The Borrower represents that the loan and any repayments are not derived from, and shall not be used for, any unlawful activity, and shall promptly notify the Lender of any change in the information furnished.

title: SARFAESI Enforcement
citations: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 s.13
text: The Parties acknowledge that the Lender is a secured creditor entitled to enforce security interests under the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (SARFAESI). Upon the account being classified as a non-performing asset and on default continuing after a notice under Section 13(2) of SARFAESI, the Lender may, without the intervention of any court or tribunal, take possession of, manage, and transfer the secured assets and exercise all rights available to a secured creditor under the Act and the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002. This clause applies only to the extent the Lender is a 'secured creditor' eligible to invoke SARFAESI (i.e. a scheduled bank or notified financial institution / NBFC); it shall not be construed to confer SARFAESI rights on a lender not so eligible.

title: Repayment (Bullet)
citations: Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.55; Indian Contract Act, 1872 s.37
text: This is a bullet (balloon) facility. The Borrower shall repay the entire Principal Amount in a single lump sum on the Maturity Date, and there shall be no scheduled amortisation of principal prior thereto. (a) Interest on the outstanding Principal Amount shall accrue and be paid by the Borrower periodically on each interest payment date specified in this Agreement until the Maturity Date, when all accrued and unpaid interest shall also fall due together with the Principal Amount. (b) The Borrower may, subject to the prepayment terms of this Agreement, prepay the Principal Amount in whole or in part before the Maturity Date. (c) Time shall be of the essence in respect of repayment, and any failure to repay the Principal Amount in full on the Maturity Date shall constitute an Event of Default entitling the Lender to exercise its rights under this Agreement. (d) All payments shall be made in Indian Rupees in immediately available cleared funds to the account notified by the Lender, free of any set-off or counterclaim and without deduction save as required by law.
